 Medicare enrollment deadline nears
 Don’t wait until it’s too late
 Published:  November 9, 2026 at 1:08 PM Tags:  wdiv , live in the d , medicare annual enrollment , insurance , healthcare , coverage , deadline , december 7 , m1 insurance group The advertiser paid a fee to promote this sponsored article and may have influenced or authored the content. The views expressed in this article are those of the advertiser and do not necessarily reflect those of this site or affiliated companies.
 As the Medicare Annual Enrollment Period winds down, a local licensed Medicare agent is urging consumers not to assume their current plan will carry over smoothly into the new year.
 Debbie Stroup, a licensed Medicare agent with M1 Insurance Group, said this time of year is critical for anyone on Medicare, even those who feel satisfied with their current coverage.
 “Because right now is the best time to take a look at that Medicare plan,” Stroup said. She explained that many people layer supplemental coverage on top of basic Medicare to fill gaps, but that an arrangement that worked well one year is not guaranteed to work the next.
 “There’s 115,000 people that are going to lose their coverage this year,” Stroup said, adding that many will not realize the change until January 1, when they may discover that doctors or medications are no longer covered under their plan.
 Stroup said the consequences of an outdated plan can show up quickly and expensively, from paying significantly more to see an out-of-network doctor to a prescription cost jumping sharply once it falls outside a plan’s coverage.
 For those who haven’t yet reviewed their coverage, Stroup said there is still time to act before the December 7 enrollment deadline. “What you want to do is gather your doctors, your prescriptions, your eye doctor, your dentist, and where your pharmacy is, and you want to make sure that all of those are still in your plan,” she said.
 She noted that M1 Insurance Group can help consumers navigate that review at no cost. “There’s no charge at all for our service,” Stroup said.
 Even for procrastinators, Stroup said missing the deadline isn’t the end of the road, there are options available in January as well. Still, she encouraged people to act sooner rather than later. “Let’s not procrastinate,” she said.
 Stroup described her role as that of an independent guide through an often-confusing system. “No insurance company do we work for,” she said. “We are here for you to make sure that you’re in that plan.”
 She said her goal is to give clients peace of mind year-round, not just during enrollment season. “We always say think about it one day a year, then 364 days you don’t have to think about Medicare at all,” Stroup said.
 For more information, M1 Insurance Group can be reached at 248-227-0347 or online at m1insurancegroup.com .
